findings.text: Hash table helpers offer bucket array setup, head insertion keyed by hashed value, membership probing, full emptiness probing, and node removal with reinitialization, with parallel regular and RCU insertion and removal paths sharing the same bucket choice.

An empty bucket is recognized by absence of a first link, an unlinked node by absence of a predecessor link, initialization clears the relevant links, and unlinking rewires predecessor and successor before optionally returning the node to the cleared state, leaving an already cleared node untouched.

Complete table walks advance a bucket index from the start through the table size and visit members of each bucket in list order, ending when all buckets have been scanned; RCU and deletion safe shapes preserve the same outer walk while changing only inner traversal guarantees.

Key focused walks compute a single bucket from the key and bit count and then traverse only that bucket, yielding members whose linkage belongs there; regular, RCU, untraced RCU, and deletion safe shapes differ only in traversal protection, not in bucket choice.
Identifier map object stores an underlying radix tree root together with a numeric base offset and a numeric next hint used to resume allocation scans.
The free identifier tag value equals zero.

Construction helpers establish an empty radix root marked as identifier owned, record a caller chosen base with zeroed cursor, provide a zero base shortcut, and allow static definition of a named instance.

Synchronization for identifier maps reuses the embedded tree lock with regular, soft interrupt, hard interrupt, and interrupt state saving pairings, each lock having a matching unlock on the same root.
Cursor accessors expose the allocation hint with single access read and write semantics for concurrent observation without full locking.
Cleanup scoped holder pairs a pointer to an identifier map with an integer identifier slot.
A null holder uses an empty map pointer with a negative identifier, and a take helper retrieves and clears a holder slot.
An identifier map counts as empty only when the underlying tree has no head and carries the free tag.
Preload teardown releases the reservation lock associated with radix preloads.

Forward scans start from a caller index and repeatedly fetch the next present entry while advancing the index, with plain, wide, resuming, and wide resuming shapes that differ in counter width and start handling but share monotonic index progress.
Bitmap chunk holds an array of machine words sized to the chunk, and allocator object wraps a single extensible array.
Chunk storage equals 128 bytes, with derived long and bit counts, and allocator initialization combines interrupt locking with allocation support, exposed through static and value initializers.
Allocation offers full range, lower bounded, and upper bounded forms funnelling into a ranged allocator, plus an initializer that prepares the embedded array with the required flags and empty head.
Emptiness means the embedded array has no head, presence of a single value is tested by an exact range search, and first value discovery searches the full unsigned range.
Interval node embeds a red black link plus inclusive start, inclusive last, and a cached subtree maximum used for pruning.
Span walk state keeps two private node references with first and last indexes, overlapping start and last views for hole versus used spans, and a signed hole marker.
Span walks begin at a caller range, repeatedly advance to the next hole or used run, and finish when the marker reaches the terminal negative value.

A generator macro yields type specialized insert, remove, subtree search, first match, and next match operations over a cached red black root for caller supplied node, link, type, and bound accessors.

Ordering follows interval start, each subtree caches the largest last below it with monotonic updates on descent and augmented rebalancing, intersection requires start ordering against the query end plus query start against node last, and empty or disjoint trees short circuit without walking.
Size helper denotes two raised to the given bit count, mask helper denotes one less than that size, and the fixed initial value equals hexadecimal deadbeef.

Hashing entry points cover arbitrary byte strings, arrays of 32 bit words, and fixed one to three word forms, each folding length and caller seed into the starting state and returning the mixed accumulator.

Block processing absorbs input into three accumulators with a mixing transformation, trailing input is folded by position into the accumulators, and a final avalanche transforms all three before the result is taken from the third.

Queue header records input and output positions with a mask, element size, and data pointer, overlaid by a union exposing typed, constant typed, record sized, and pointer views, with inline storage, pointer storage, and one or two byte record variants.

Declaration helpers create inline or pointer queues, initialization zeroes positions and derives mask, element size, and data location from the storage shape, and static definition precomputes the same header state.

Mask presence signals initialization, size is one more than mask, element and record sizes derive from storage types, reset clears both positions, and small integer helpers pass values through for checked contexts.
Each header defines a single inclusion guard macro marking its translation unit as seen.

Traversal safety depends on caller choice among regular, RCU, and deletion safe forms with no automatic fallback, cursor and hint values use single access without full mutual exclusion, and static queue sizes outside power of two provoke a compile time sized error.

Callable entry points for other subsystems include table setup and membership operations, identifier and allocator setup with cursor and emptiness handling, interval span walking, byte and word hashing, and queue declaration with reset and size queries.
